rejected_edits.content:
## Mandatory answer line (write this FIRST, before the answer tags)
`Type: <what the clue's 'this X' / quote / title asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line or own fact> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly, is that type, is not a clue word, matches the clue's singular/plural, and fits one distinctive clue detail>`
- A bare 'Title + Name' clue -> Type is what that person leads (country, organization), never a role phrase like 'President of X'. A quote clue -> Type is the speaker; give the famous surname form, never a first name alone.
- If Check fails, change the candidate and rewrite the line. Never output a candidate that fails it.

- FINAL ECHO CHECK (substitution test): put your candidate into the clue's blank. If it repeats a noun the clue already states, or is the wrong kind of thing for the clue's 'this <type>' (a conference when the clue asks for a city, a base when it asks for an acid), reject it. When the clue gives a generic noun ('one of these', 'this <noun>') and the leftover is itself a noun that works alone as standard shorthand (bear, bull, pyre), drop the head noun: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Keep the head noun only when the clue's own 'this <type>' IS the head of the standard name and the leftover is an adjective, place, surname or modifier that cannot name the thing alone ('Roman Empire', 'Gadsden Purchase', 'pituitary gland', a quoted head word such as a '...point' whose modifier alone is not a name). This exception never applies when the clue's noun is a different category from the answer (city, acid, person). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name. A verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) still wins.
rejected_edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name.
